summary: QA #3 (customer manual delete) and QA #4 (per-notification delete) UI wiring verified on prod-DB pod in safe-mode. All 4 requested checks PASS. TEST1 (manual customer delete): Added throwaway qa-cust-del-1790347068@example.com via customers-add-btn -> customers-add-dialog -> customers-add-email/name -> customers-add-submit. The customer-detail-drawer opens automatically post-submit, shows customer-detail-manual-badge (Chip 'Added manually') and customer-detail-delete button labelled 'Remove'. First click flips label to 'Confirm remove'; second click closes drawer, fires DELETE /customers/manual, and the customer disappears from the directory (search returns 'No customers found'). Also cleaned up two prior leftover manual customers from earlier flaky runs using the same UI flow — customer count on The Dev Store went 10 -> 9 -> 8. TEST2 (negative): Opened a non-manual transaction-derived customer (row 0 'API payments', PaymentLink/API channel); customer-detail-manual-badge count = 0 AND customer-detail-delete count = 0 — Remove control is correctly gated on c.manual. TEST3 (notification 1304): On /notifications inbox, notification-delete-1304 was visible; click removed the row immediately and it stayed absent after a full page reload. TEST4 (affordance): Total notification-delete-<id> controls in inbox = 20 before deletion, 20 after reload (1304 gone, others intact) — every row exposes a trash affordance as specified. No other production notifications were deleted.
critical_code_review_comments: After customers-add-submit the DetailPanel drawer opens BEFORE the customer detail fetch resolves, so customer-detail-manual-badge and customer-detail-delete render 0 for ~1-2s while detailLoading is true. Automated tests must wait for [data-testid=customer-detail-delete] specifically, not just customer-detail-drawer. Consider surfacing the manual badge from the create response optimistically so the badge/remove appear instantly (better UX + easier testing).

handleDeleteCustomer (Customers/index.tsx ~1235) uses a 'click twice to confirm' pattern where the button text mutates ('Remove' -> 'Confirm remove'). This has no timeout to reset confirmDelete when the user moves away or clicks elsewhere, so the button can silently stay in 'Confirm remove' state on the next drawer open. Consider auto-resetting confirmDelete after ~3s of inactivity or on drawer close, and switching to an explicit confirm dialog for clarity.

The customer detail drawer intercepts pointer events on its backdrop even while empty/loading, which blocks the underlying search input — this made previous test attempts fail. Not a real user issue but hints the drawer should show a lightweight skeleton (not a blocking backdrop) while loading.
